customManagers.description: Update ARGs annotated with '# renovate: datasource=… depName=…'. Needed because the base images compose multiple ARGs in FROM (e.g. ${REGISTRY_DOCKERHUB}/library/rust:${RUST_VERSION}-slim-bookworm), which the dockerfile manager cannot auto-replace. Two matchStrings because ARGs come in two shapes, and the digest has to be captured SEPARATELY: the original single pattern captured '0.3.2@sha256:…' as one currentValue, which no versioning scheme can parse — so every digest-pinned ARG in the repo (cve-gate's three bases, ci-runner's CVE_GATE_VERSION and RUNNER_VERSION) was silently unmanaged. First pattern: ARGs whose value ends ':<tag>@<digest>' or is '<version>@<digest>'. Second: bare versions with no digest, digest-containing values excluded so the two patterns never both match.

Update tool versions that composite actions pass as INPUT DEFAULTS (syft, cosign). Renovate's action manager pins the `uses:` ref but is blind to a version string handed to that action via `with:` — which is how syft sat on v1.21.0 from 2026-06-16 until v1.48.0 shipped, with nothing watching it.

packageRules.description: These Dockerfiles compose their FROM refs from multiple ARGs; the dockerfile manager resolves the ARGs at extraction but then cannot find the resolved string in the raw file ('Cannot find replaceString' → the whole branch silently produces no commit). The annotated-ARG custom manager above owns these deps instead.

The release toolchain (webgrip/workflows ADR-0005) is the one npm dependency set in this repo that is LOCKED, because it decides every repo's version numbers. These package.json files are also their image's release manifest — Renovate owns the dependencies; semantic-release owns the version. It upgrades as ONE reviewed PR across all three images — they must stay on the same semantic-release version, since the derived images replace the base's tree wholesale. A MAJOR bump is expected to FAIL the image build: each Dockerfile asserts the major that webgrip/workflows' composites target.
Annotated ARGs hold bare versions that are reused outside the FROM line (rustup default, tag suffix composition); appending @sha256 digests would corrupt them.

techdocs-builder's python env is pip-compile hash-locked (requirements*.in -> .txt, compiled for python:3.13-alpine). Renovate re-runs the header command to refresh locks+hashes. mkdocs-techdocs-core pins most of the mkdocs universe with == constraints, so most transitive 'updates' are impossible until techdocs-core itself bumps — expect small PRs. zensical lives in a SEPARATE lock (requirements-zensical) because it cannot coexist with techdocs-core (pymdown-extensions conflict).

webgrip/workflows is pinned by commit SHA with a '# main' branch annotation — the repo cuts no tags, so Renovate's tag lookup 404s (GET /repos/webgrip/workflows/tags/main) and the FATAL aborts the ENTIRE repo run, taking every other update (including all annotated-ARG bumps) down with it. The pin is moved deliberately by hand when the reusables change; Renovate has nothing to version here.
